transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-11
Time: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~52 mins
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE); Maya Singh (Redwood SE); Liam O'Connor (Redwood Solutions); Priya Menon (Head of ML, Apex); Tom Alvarez (CTO); Jorge Rivera (Platform Eng)

Auto-summary (auto-generated):
- Need: multi-lingual customer support and document parsing for shipments in 6 languages, heavy long-context jobs for multi-document tracing (~25-40k tokens), and tool-calling to invoke internal shipment DBs and external rate APIs.
- Consideration: evaluate open models (Llama variants, Mistral-style, MPT) for latency/cost; dedicated pools for predictable throughput, private deployment for PII; Redwood to provide bench results and pricing.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ethan: Hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Ethan from Redwood, with Maya our systems engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:07] Priya: Good thanks, excited to dig in. we've been looking at several open models and trying to figure out latency and cost tradeoffs.
[00:12] Tom: yep quick intro, i'm Tom, CTO, we'll mostly listen and Priya and Jorge will ask the nitty gritty.
[00:20] Maya: great quick agenda, model selection, context length needs, multilingual, tool-calling, and then deployment options (hosted/dedicated/private) and next steps. sound good?
[00:28] Priya: sounds good. to start, our primary use case is customer support summarization and multi-doc tracing for shipment disputes. typical convo + document context ends up around 20-35k tokens. Occasionally we have 60k token bundles but that's rare.
[00:40] Jorge: we also need to call internal APIs — order lookup, billing — and trigger rate-estimates from a third-party. tool-calling is a hard requirement.
[00:49] Maya: ok so two main constraints: long context (20-40k typical) and deterministic tool-calling. do you have latency SLOs?
[00:56] Priya: for chat responses we want p95 under 700ms ideally; for the long batch legal/trace jobs we can accept a few seconds but cost matters.
[01:08] Ethan: got it. a few things to flag — many open models have tradeoffs: smaller quantized LLaMA-like weights cost less but vary on context-window support and tooling for function calls. Mistral-ish models are strong for generation but you'll want to check for long-context performance; MPT and some of the long-context tuned variants are promising.
[01:27] [Speaker 3]: i'm sorry could you repeat which models you mentioned?
[01:29] Maya: sure, Llama variants (eg 2-13b fine-tuned/quantized), Mistral-family, MPT and long-context tuned versions like LlamaX/Longformer style variants. also some customers use fragmented approaches — short context generation with streaming + external KV cache for older tokens.
[01:46] Tom: what about tool-calling? we need robust function calling, schema enforcement, and deterministic invocation so we don't accidentally call billing with malformed params.
[01:56] Maya: Redwood supports structured function/tool calling in the API; the runtime can enforce schemas and we surface logs/traces per call. caveat is some older open models don't natively support function-token semantics so we do an orchestration layer that normalizes outputs and validates before invoking. there can be small latencies for that transform but it's usually <50-100ms.
[02:15] Priya: and encryption / compliance — we're dealing with PII on shipments. do you provide KMS integration and can we run private?
[02:23] Ethan: yes we have private deployment options (VPC/on-prem) with KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs. we can also do Dedicated pools if you want isolation but with Redwood-managed infra, or a Private control plane for full customer-managed networking. both are SOC 2 compliant, i'll share the security packet.
[02:37] Jorge: any differences in model availability across hosted vs private?
[02:41] Maya: generally same catalog, but very large or experimental builds sometimes require specific infra; quantized versions are available across deployments but some 100k-context variants may require custom backends or more memory — we can surface compatible variants.
[02:55] Tom: what's the sweet spot for cost vs latency for a 30k token context?
[03:00] Maya: short answer: you either pay for memory and GPU to keep the KV cache hot (dedicated or private, bigger GPUs) which lowers latency, or you use hosted with autoscaling and occasional cold starts that bump latencies and maybe increase per-token cost. for many customers we recommend a dedicated pool for consistent p95 latency with long contexts. quantized int8/4 can reduce costs 2-4x but can impact quality on certain prompts.
[03:25] Priya: do you have benchmark numbers? like p95 and cost for 30k on a few model candidates?
[03:30] Ethan: we can run a benchmark for you — Maya will schedule a deep-dive. we typically run against a 10k prompt set to estimate TCO and latency distribution. we'll include Llama-2-style 70B quantized, Mistral large, MPT long-context tuned and a Redwood-verified 32k variant.
[03:49] [00:03:50] Jorge: how about multilingual — we support English plus Spanish and Portuguese and occasionally Mandarin; do the models handle this natively?
[03:58] Maya: many open models have solid multilingual coverage, but performance varies — some need fine-tuning for technical logistics terms. we recommend evaluation on your real utterances. also note tokenization differences may increase token counts in non-latin scripts.
[04:14] Tom: for tool-calling and privacy, can the tool payloads be encrypted end-to-end or at least masked in logs?
[04:20] Ethan: yes we have data-handling controls — ability to mask fields in logs, redact PII before persistent storage, and KMS for data at rest. for private deployments you can ensure logs never leave your VPC.
[04:31] Priya: great. do you recommend hosted to get started or go straight to dedicated?
[04:36] Maya: common pattern: start hosted to iterate on prompts and flows, then move to dedicated for production throughput and latency SLOs. if regulatory constraints demand, we can start private. for your PII-heavy workflows, a pilot on dedicated with strict logging and KMS is a reasonable path.
[04:51] Tom: what about model rollouts — we want canary and safe fallback if quality regresses.
[04:56] Maya: Redwood Console supports rollouts, canary, A/B, and automatic fallback to a smaller model if the variant fails. plus eval hooks so you can tie regressions to a prompt set.
[05:07] [Speaker 4]: sorry quick question, you mentioned KV cache — what is that exactly?
[05:10] Maya: KV cache is the offloaded key-value attention cache for autoregressive models — we use it to avoid reprocessing the full sequence every token and we can persist prefixes for repeated contexts. some customers call it K-V cash or K-V cache, transcription sometimes says K-V cash — it's the same.
[05:24] Priya: ok that helps. for our large batch jobs (60k tokens) is it feasible to stitch multiple contexts or do we need a single 100k window?
[05:31] Ethan: depends on the workflow — stitching with external retrieval and a hybrid approach (shorter context generation + retrieval of older segments) is often more cost-effective than maintaining a single 100k context; but if you need absolute global coherence, we can explore long-context variants with specialized backends.
[05:48] Jorge: what about caching / prefix reuse across similar shipments?
[05:52] Maya: Redwood can persist KV prefixes per customer/session to speed up repeat work and reduce token re-processing — saves token cost and latency.
[05:59] Tom: any gotchas with function calling and schema enforcement? e.g., models hallucinating fields or returning malformed JSON.
[06:06] Maya: yes hallucinations happen; we run output validators and a sandbox step that validates against the schema, and we have deterministic retries and guardrails. in some cases we implement a small L0 parser using a stricter model or heuristics before calling the real API.
[06:20] Priya: okay pricing — for dedicated, what's the ballpark monthly for the capacity we'd need?
[06:25] Ethan: high-level we can estimate after the benchmark. ballpark for a small dedicated pool supporting your concurrency might be mid-five figures monthly; exact depends on model choice, peak concurrency, and context length. we'll send a TCO spreadsheet.
[06:39] [00:06:40] Tom: do you support on-prem air-gapped?
[06:43] Maya: yes we have an on-prem package for air-gapped deployment; that typically involves more lead time for ops and a license + support commitment.
[06:52] Priya: ok next steps then?
[06:55] Ethan: we'll send pricing and TCO + security packet by Friday. Maya will schedule a 90-min deep-dive bench session where we'll run the 10k prompt set and measure p95, p50, and cost. Priya will share the sample prompts and top production cases.
[07:08] Jorge: sounds good. one more thing — latency SLO at p95 700ms is pretty aggressive for 30k contexts, right?
[07:15] Maya: it's aggressive unless you have dedicated hot GPU memory and careful quantization; we'll surface realistic p95 numbers in the bench.
[07:23] Tom: ok thanks everyone.
[07:26] Ethan: thanks all we'll follow up with notes and next steps.
